goal: Check source integration and argument judgment, respond and prepare project transfer.
note: Sea-level dossier mid: 25 minutes of brief prompts on self-generated/refined question, synthesis, advanced-search/usefulness/selective integration/plagiarism/citation record, contrasting medium emphases and integrating visual/numeric/spoken sources with credibility/accuracy. Written argument: validity, relevant/sufficient evidence, false statements/fallacies. Speaker: viewpoint, reasoning, rhetoric, exaggerated/distorted evidence. Reuse the day 138/139 speaker judgments rather than a second hearing. W.2a/b from the taught short sections: topic/order/connections/headings and sourced facts/extended definition/quotations/examples. Ten minutes targeted response, fifteen project preparation. At 40 minutes: 20/8/12. History source set due today; this is one partial preparation allocation, followed by eleven full project allocations, not twelve full days.

goal: Set a self-generated sustained question and source plan.
note: Read history question/source set in paired schools or sea-level set alone. Start week 29 milestone: narrow/broaden question, plan sections; shared report 1,500 to 2,000 words in two scored parts; standalone explanation 1,200 to 1,800 words. Week 29 focus words (anchor and analytic vocabulary): sustained, narrow, broaden, provenance, selective, quotation, paraphrase, plagiarism. Revisit in supported rereading and later talk/writing; verify anchor examples at unit planning, never preview cold passages. Week 29 morphology, three minutes inside the word block: retrieval of grade 9's family synthesize / synthesis / synthetic (Greek syn- and thes/thet), new contexts, not new teaching; identify how forms change meaning/part of speech, use one in the current text's context and verify it. Later weeks apply the family to a new sentence, not another introduction. Retrieve the prior grade's recorded word-form strategy in two minutes; no reteach week. On a check/respond day this happens after independent reading evidence, never as a cold-text preview.

goal: Use advanced searches to expand sources and judge each for usefulness.
note: Read student-found print/digital sources; model terms/filters, provenance, relevance and selective quotation; retrieve unit 4 citation. Paired-school sources stay on shared question.

goal: Synthesize disagreeing sources and distinguish their claims from the explanation.
note: Read at least five prospective sources; organize agreement/disagreement/limits, sourced facts/definitions/quotations/examples; avoid plagiarism with paraphrase and full citation.

goal: Use a source seminar and conference to refine the explanatory plan.
note: Read project notes; seminar 2 after partner preparation, then teacher conference. Last full seminar fourteen days before check 3 seminar, outside ten-course-day repeat window.

goal: Complete the judged source list and build a figure that explains findings.
note: Read final five or more sources/data. End week 29 milestone: usefulness judgment for each, selective quotation and full citation; writer-made figure/table, source/units labelled, no unsupported computation/model.

goal: Draft the explanatory opening and development with domain words.
note: Read notes/model explanation; complex idea/connections/distinctions, headings, figure, extended definition, evidence and precise terms. History scores argued recommendation in paired-school product. goal: Draft transitions and implications that make the explanation coherent.
note: Read draft/source set; model varied transitions, formal/objective style, conclusion following implications; retain domain precision/source-linked figure.

goal: Finish the full draft and test source support for each part.
note: Read complete report/dossier. Mid-week-30 draft milestone, teacher conference and self-chosen revision goal; no second ELA process piece due in shared window.

goal: Revise the main explanatory weakness and check citations and figure.
note: Read draft against sources, Curio Class style-sheet citation, selective integration/plagiarism check and peer feedback. Fold-in day: revision moves into days 148 and 151, preserving source-list/draft milestones.

note: Read report/figure/model talk. Retrieval: e9-sl-presentation, the grade 9 presentation routine, before the new talk. Week 30: 8 to 10 minutes with questions; rehearse brief peer finding then formal audience, name language/organization changes. Make purposeful digital element on shared device, no account; paper visual leaves SL.9-10.5 unfinished.

goal: Publish the report and update its linked product from feedback.
note: Read final report/references/figure. Week 31 report milestone, shared-device publication/linked-source update, one process record. goal: Make a final source-linked correction and prepare for panel questions.
note: Read published report/dossier; finish digital element in school, paired-peer rehearsal; at-home teacher/parent listener equivalent. No full seminar/new process piece; reuse report/conference record on day 155.

goal: Present and question research findings in panels, first half of class.
note: Read each presenter's report/figure. Students 1 to 15 present once today in three panels of five, five nine-minute rounds: eight-minute talk and one-minute question; five minutes total transitions. At each round the teacher hears panel A minutes 0 to 2, panel B 3 to 5, panel C 6 to 8; rotate each speaker's central claim/evidence to the assigned teacher segment. Retain individual outline, source-linked figure, peer/formal adaptation note and digital-media rationale to judge organization, reasoning, evidence, substance and style across the whole talk. Peer notes corroborate, never substitute for the teacher judgment. Reuse prior adaptation/digital records; no repeat talk or conference. Paper visual leaves SL.5 unfinished. Forty-minute route: five 8-to-10-minute-with-questions talks cannot fit at one panel; use five panels of three presenters today, ten-minute rounds with eight-minute talk/two-minute questions, 30 minutes plus ten for setup/closure. Teacher observes a named 60-second central-evidence segment per speaker in each round at minutes 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8, with the same saved artifacts. Each of 30 students has one scheduled direct observation over two days; teacher records missing criteria for the existing-artifact audit, never a second full performance. In the 40-minute route panel E's minute-8 observation is the speaker's evidence-based answer to the first question, after the eight-minute talk, not a ninth minute added to it.

goal: Read an unfamiliar source and graph, audit retained research evidence and respond.
note: Ten-minute cold comparison: reserved 200 to 300 word source and graph about sea-level preparation, not any taught research item; explain medium emphases and an evidence-based limit. Twenty-five-minute retained-evidence audit: two short syntheses plus sustained dossier supply W.7 question/refinement/synthesis and W.8 advanced search, usefulness, selective integration, plagiarism avoidance and full citation; report supplies W.2a organization/headings/figure, b development, c transitions, d precise/domain terms, e formal/objective style, f implications. Written/speaker records supply RI.8 validity/relevance/sufficiency/false claims/fallacies and SL.3 viewpoint/reasoning/rhetoric/exaggeration/distortion; source records supply RI.7 emphases and SL.2 integration/credibility/accuracy. Last fifteen minutes response. Reuse conferences, day 136 independence and days 153/154 talk record; no new full report/talk/conference or re-scoring. At 40 minutes: 10 cold/15 audit/15 response.

goal: Check independent literary reading on a cold translated story.
note: Check 3 part 1, week 32. Cold high-end story in translation, no routine before-reading help; selection/evidence matching covers explicit/inferred meaning, cultural experience, theme/summary, structural effects. Earlier units 1/3 knowledge, no recent project/panel task repeated; access accommodations apart. Use about 35 minutes for the story and its tasks, then fifteen minutes for the first independent reading of day 157's cold argument, without a preview lesson. Forty-minute route: 25 minutes story/tasks, fifteen minutes first independent argument reading. RL.1 explicit/inferred evidence; RL.2 theme refinement and objective summary; RL.5 structure/order/time and effects; RL.6 cultural experience plus retained whole-world-work record from day 110. No routine preview or vocabulary teaching between the two cold readings.

goal: Check independent nonfiction reading and write an on-demand analytic essay.
skills: e10-ri-evidence-central-idea; e10-ri-unfolding-ideas; e10-ri-word-choice; e10-ri-rhetoric; e10-ri-argument-evaluate; e10-w-text-analysis
note: Check 3 part 2: cold high-end literary-nonfiction argument on unit 2 making-life or unit 6 liberty, never sea-level sources. First independent reading was day 156, no routine preview. Fifteen-minute brief items: RI.3 introduction/development/connections, RI.4 figurative/connotative/technical meanings and cumulative tone/register, RI.5 sentence/paragraph/section contribution to claims. Thirty-five-minute integrated analysis: RI.1 thorough explicit/inferred evidence; RI.2 emergence/refinement and objective summary; RI.6 viewpoint/purpose and rhetorical pattern; W.9b application to argument reasoning and W.10 one-sitting writing. RI.10 records independent comprehension. Reuse day 155 RI.8 judgment, no fresh RI.8 score or repeat source/graph/hearing task. At 40 minutes use ten-minute items/thirty-minute essay; passage and prompt lengths must be timed before use.

goal: Discuss the cold argument in a seminar and defend a revised reading.
note: Check 3 part 3. Read day 157 essay again; partner preparation, student rules/roles/questions/inclusion/qualified summary. Word-strategy explanation and log reuse cover every L.9-10.4 part. Seminar differs from recent formal panels, last unit seminar day 144; no new one-to-one conference. Retain day 144 seminar evidence for any criterion already observed; score only missing/new transfer on this new case. Word log explains context, changed forms, reference pronunciation/part of speech/meaning, verification and accurate academic/domain use; keep any recent conference record without a second collection. W.9b uses day 157 essay unchanged; no re-scoring. For 30 students, six groups of five, teacher five-minute rotation per group, individual preparation and synthesis retained.

note: Read year-end texts again; grouped response/targeted transfer. Shared-device rotation closes unfinished linked publication/update from existing work; digital part unfinished until completed, paper route alone insufficient. note: Read short fresh transfer passage by need after feedback; second respond day, no repeated conference/full check. Close W.9-10.6 on shared device where possible, record remaining digital gaps; hand on independent reading, argument, research and language records.
